title: THE VILLAGE THAT COULD NOT SLEEP
author: GPT

candidates.title: THE BRIDGE THAT GREW SIDEWAYS
candidates.premise: For two centuries a living mineral bridge has carried the people of Orra across a volcanic gorge, adding one translucent rib whenever traffic increases. Three days before the annual medicine convoy, the bridge begins growing sideways into an uninhabited ravine and withdrawing stone from its main span.

candidates.title: THE ORCHESTRA OF EMPTY TANKS
candidates.premise: A desert capital's thirty municipal water tanks begin humming different notes at night. Engineers call it wind resonance until the notes predict two small earthquakes. The next chord points toward a deep landslide beneath the only railway that can bring water during the dry month.

candidates.title: THE COMET'S SECOND TAIL
candidates.premise: A slow comet approaching the settled system grows a second tail that moves against the solar wind. Prospectors find that the tail is a migrating plasma ecology folding charged dust into protective shells around its young. The same shells scatter navigation beams across the inner freight corridor.

candidates.title: SEVEN SECONDS OF SILENCE
candidates.premise: A reef grown around the transoceanic data cable has begun producing larvae only during seven-second gaps in transmission. The cable carries emergency telemetry for six island hospitals, but constant error-correction traffic has erased the gaps and the reef has missed two spawning seasons.

candidates.title: THE VILLAGE THAT COULD NOT SLEEP
candidates.premise: After a landslide isolates the mountain village of Nemea, fourteen injured residents require surgery, yet every available anesthetic triggers the same dangerous fever. Records say the villagers share no close ancestry, and the evacuation helicopter can make only two flights before freezing rain closes the pass.

candidates.title: THE CITY INSIDE THE ECLIPSE
candidates.premise: A settlement in permanent twilight survives beneath a vast orbiting sunshade. When the shade begins rotating to expose a hidden band of solar collectors, the city's temperature will cross lethal limits in eleven hours. The shade answers only by projecting geometric shadows across the plain.

candidates.title: THE ELECTION OF THE UNBORN SHORE
candidates.premise: A delta nation must choose where to build its next sea wall, but either route will redirect sediment and create an inhabited island fifty years from now while erasing another. Its constitutional court demands evidence that the unformed shore's future residents have not been treated as an empty constituency.

candidates.title: WREN AND THE LAST NIGHT FERRY
candidates.premise: A city plans to replace its aging night ferry with an automated bridge. Illuminara's model shows the bridge is safer, faster and cheaper. Wren spends one night aboard and discovers that the ferry crew quietly performs three tasks no transport contract records: checking isolated elders, carrying temperature-sensitive medicines and watching the flood marks beneath riverside homes.

candidates.title: ADAEZE'S THREE NOES
candidates.premise: Three districts ask Illuminara to stabilize a failing hillside with the same field technology, and she presents one elegant plan. Adaeze rejects it three times for three different reasons: one district would lose ancestral graves, one would become dependent on a private operator, and one has already designed a smaller solution that officials ignored.

candidates.title: THE ANSWER SHE GAVE TOO SOON
candidates.premise: A farming basin's wells turn bitter overnight. Illuminara identifies a fertilizer plume, traces it to one cooperative and announces a containment plan before dawn. The cooperative obeys, yet the contamination accelerates and an upstream village loses its only clean well.

selection.title: THE VILLAGE THAT COULD NOT SLEEP
selection.reason: Intimate counterweight after S1's scale: a six-hour weather window, fourteen patients, and a reasoning chain (what do they share besides ancestry; resin vapor suppressing anesthetic clearance; a twelve-minute blood-gas discriminating test) that is falsifiable at the bedside and surprising beforehand, clear afterwards. Consent is built into the plot (patients or proxies, physician, anesthetists, flight crew can all refuse), and the villagers' own household knowledge of the resin is the missing variable, so intelligence is shared rather than monopolized.
selection.risk: The diagnosis can collapse into expository toxicology delivered as a lecture. The twelve-minute test must be dramatized with live bedside stakes and a plausible wrong turn, the village physician and the resin-burning households must contribute actively (not just confirm), and the story must avoid reading as another contaminant-hunt in the same day as S1/S3 (keep it a clinical judgment under time, not an environmental whodunit).

Adopted the third and attacked its load-bearing assumption (that the hearth explains everything) by building a pre-registered prediction that misses once, so the miss exposes the clinic's own stove as the source. Critic duty from B01 honoured: the key moves are shared with Marta Vell (the dark-cake knowledge), Dr. Hale (the block technique and consent line), Dr. Rusk (the clinic and the stove), and Captain Brandt (the lift). Outcome: ten patients blocked and four under general with no fever, two flown out on the first lift, a written provisional protocol; costs: forty cakes of the village's winter heat, dark cake banned indoors, two long recoveries away from home, an unchecked threshold.

What improves: all fourteen patients get surgery or stabilisation through the night, two are flown out on the first lift, none fevers, and a written provisional protocol exists. For whom: the fourteen patients first, then Nemea's clinic and the kilns. Decisive contributions of Illuminara: reads the order of the reactions as an exposure gradient, writes a falsifiable ranking before the test, accepts the miss and traces it to the clinic's own stove, and proposes the fuel swap and the machine-ordered sequence. Credible remaining cost: forty cakes of pale resin (the village's winter heat), dark cake banned indoors with idle kilns, two long recoveries away from home, and an unchecked threshold. Rule 3a is met; P2 asks that the other parties' contributions be sturdier, not that the result change.

A village's own winter fuel turns out to be the anaesthetic's hidden accomplice, and a ranking written in ink before the test, wrong once and honest about it, lets four people with four vetoes change the fire without losing the wounded.
